assumptions: Double-digit growth in non-seasonal portfolio applied to all quarters, with seasonal quarters showing modest YoY growth
OPM for Q1 and Q4 maintained at 18% (lower end of aspirational 17-18% range), Q2 and Q3 mirror historical seasonal margins
Amortization of acquired brands continues to impact PAT, with gradual normalization by Q4FY27

projection.rationale: Q1 is historically a strong quarter (18-23% OPM). Revenue guided for double-digit growth in non-seasonal portfolio, but Q1FY26 base of 861 Cr already high; 4.5% YoY growth reflects steady non-seasonal momentum partially offset by seasonal normalization. OPM at 18% aligns with aspirational long-term margin and Q1FY26 level.

Q2 is historically the weakest quarter (3.3-4.0% OPM). Revenue projected at 680 Cr, a 4.6% YoY increase over Q2FY26's 650 Cr, reflecting double-digit non-seasonal growth offset by seasonal mix. OPM maintained at 4% consistent with historical Q2 levels. PAT negative due to continued amortization of acquired brands and seasonal operating deleverage.

drivers.label: Scale Increase
drivers.value: Operating leverage starting to play out

projection.rationale: Q3 shows seasonal improvement with revenue at 1020 Cr (5.7% YoY growth over Q3FY26's 965 Cr). OPM at 6.3% mirrors Q3FY26, as margin pressure from seasonal mix and fixed cost absorption persists. PAT remains negative due to amortization and one-off costs, but improves sequentially as scale increases.

drivers.label: Margin Recovery
drivers.value: Gross margins healthy, fixed cost absorption improves

projection.rationale: Q4 is the strongest seasonal quarter. Revenue at 1560 Cr (5.1% YoY growth over Q4FY26's 1485 Cr) reflects double-digit non-seasonal growth and seasonal recovery. OPM at 18% aligns with aspirational long-term margin. PAT normalizes to 170 Cr as one-off costs fade and operating leverage benefits materialize.

deepdive.sec: Wellness FMCG / Functional Nutrition & Digital-First D2C

bull_bear.body: Strategic acquisition of Comfort Click funded via low-cost bridge loan (GBP) refinanced to Euro facility. Continued investment in R&D for new product launches (RTD, skincare variants). Divestment/liquidation of non-core subsidiary (Naturell India).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Weather dependency for ~30% of portfolio (Glucon-D/Nycil) causing quarterly volatility; Integration risks with international D2C operations; Currency fluctuation (GBP/EUR vs INR) impacting translated earnings; Intense competition in protein snacking and skincare segments; Regulatory changes in labor codes affecting cost structure.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural growth drivers and portfolio diversification benefits; Pragmatic about short-term weather-related misses; Emphasizing data-driven decision making and AI-led marketing efficiency; Committed to profitable growth over blunt volume expansion.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'seasonal' drag is masking a fundamentally stronger underlying business where normalized PAT grew 17% in Q4. The Comfort Click acquisition is already EPS accretive within 7 months, faster than typical integration timelines. Quick commerce is not just a channel but a strategic moat, contributing nearly half of all e-commerce sales and favoring Zydus's premium, small-pack, and impulse-buy SKUs over traditional general trade competitors.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Domestic: +1.7% YoY (Seasonal -9.8%, Skin/Hair +39.7%, Food/Nutrition +9.4%). International (incl. Comfort Click): +31.4% YoY like-for-like. Comfort Click: EPS accretive in Q4, expanding into new European markets plus US/UAE bets. RiteBite: Outperforming with >2x pre-acquisition CAGR, expanding into RTD beverages and chips. Everyuth: Double-digit growth driven by tan removal segment. Sugar Free: Market share +24 bps, D'lite range showing high double-digit growth.

EBITDA margin pressure stems from high fixed cost absorption in underperforming seasonal units and increased amortization of intangible assets from acquisitions. One-time costs include new labor code implementation and Naturell India liquidation. Management expects operating leverage to play out as scale increases and seasonal volatility normalizes.

outlook.body: N/A - FMCG business model driven by distribution reach and inventory turnover rather than order book. Quick commerce contribution at 7-8% of total domestic sales, representing 44-45% of e-commerce channel.

outlook.body: Geographic expansion of Comfort Click into US/UAE; Category expansion for RiteBite (RTD, chips) and Glucon-D (performance hydration 'Recharge'); New brand 'Cuticolor' in derma-supported hair color; Deepening quick commerce penetration which favors their premium/on-the-go portfolio.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Zydus Wellness delivered robust top-line growth (62% YoY) driven by the Comfort Click acquisition and strong performance in skin/protein segments, though reported PAT declined 5.8% due to one-off amortization and labor code impacts. The core narrative remains the successful de-risking of weather-dependent seasonal brands through high-margin digital-first international and domestic adjacencies, with operating leverage expected to re-accelerate once seasonal headwinds normalize.

The Company will focus on deepening market penetration, optimising supply chain efficiencies, strengthening channel partnerships and expanding its digital footprint to enhance reach and consumer accessibility across geographies.

Continue building the Company's position in Vitamins, Minerals and Supplements, a category aligned with preventive healthcare and wellness trends and a natural extension of its science-led capabilities.

Scale sustainable wellness offerings globally in the digital vitamins, minerals and supplements space on the back of the Comfort Click platform.
Maintain a strong new product pipeline out of the R&D facility at Ahmedabad, to be launched at an appropriate time based on market requirements and consumer needs.

Having transitioned from a distribution-led model to direct relationships with all modern trade and e-commerce partners, the Company continues to increase focus on organised trade with channel-specific offerings.

risks.note: A significant portion of the Company's revenue is derived from a few key brands; any disruption in supply, quality, competitive positioning or loss of consumer confidence in these brands could adversely impact business performance, growth momentum and market share. Mitigated through brand rejuvenation, continuous innovation, sustained marketing investment and portfolio diversification into adjacent offerings under established brand platforms.
risks.risk: Dependence on a few key brands

risks.note: Performance of brands such as Glucon-D and Nycil is significantly influenced by the timely onset and intensity of the Indian summer; any delay, shortening or shift in seasonal conditions may impact demand, sales volumes and inventory management. Mitigated through a flexible supply chain, improved forecasting, inventory optimisation and by deliberately reducing the saliency of seasonal products and acquiring non-seasonal portfolios.
risks.risk: Seasonal demand variability and climate-related risk

risks.note: Failure to meet standards established by regulatory authorities may result in regulatory actions, product recalls, penalties or litigation from customers, and the Company faces potential litigation risk relating to product claims made to consumers. Managed via a quality and compliance framework, global food safety standards, self-inspection, a dedicated regulatory affairs team and product-recall insurance.
risks.risk: Product quality, regulatory compliance and product-claim litigation

risks.note: Strong brand equity exposes the Company to unauthorised or illegitimate use of its brand name, packaging designs and other IP by third parties; counterfeit manufacture and distribution threaten brand credibility and can cause loss of sales, dilution of brand equity and erosion of consumer trust. Addressed through systematic IP registrations, market monitoring, timely legal action and distribution-network awareness.
risks.risk: Intellectual property misuse and counterfeit products

risks.note: Exposure to international trade disputes, protectionist policies, sudden tariff/duty changes and non-tariff barriers, plus political instability, military conflicts, currency volatility and inflation, can raise input and freight costs, disrupt supply chains and restrict market access. Mitigated through diversification of sourcing and manufacturing locations, localisation of manufacturing to reduce FX exposure, portfolio diversification and calibrated geographic expansion into relatively stable, high-potential markets.

The supply network is exposed to physical disruptions, environmental or industrial accidents, labour unrest, trade restrictions and operational challenges at key suppliers, which may impact manufacturing efficiency, logistics and timely delivery. Mitigated through an adaptive and distributed manufacturing footprint, diversified sourcing, inventory buffers and multiple sourcing options for critical inputs.

Certain categories the Company operates in remain under-penetrated, which may challenge growth aspirations in the near term through slower adoption rates, extended consumer education cycles and higher investment required for category expansion - while also representing the long-term growth opportunity.
risks.risk: Under-penetration of categories and market development burden

risks.note: Consumer healthcare and wellness products depend heavily on consumer trust; adverse publicity from misinformation, regulatory scrutiny, influencer backlash or social media controversy can rapidly impact brand perception, consumer confidence and sales. Managed through a crisis communication and response framework and active monitoring of digital platforms and online sentiment.
risks.risk: Consumer trust, brand reputation and media-related risk
